title: What is each block for?

prereqs.why: Each pairing is a primitive in the fabric and the job it exists to do.

statement:
The building blocks you are given on an FPGA, and what each one is for. Pair them up.

One description on the right belongs to a block that is not in the list — it is the one that connects the chip to the world outside it.
hints: Two of these could in principle be built out of the general-purpose logic. They exist as dedicated blocks because doing so would be wasteful — ask which two, and of what.
One of them is the only reason a design can have state at all. Without it you have combinational logic and nothing else.
One of them carries no data whatsoever.

right: A hardened multiply-accumulate unit, because building a wide multiplier out of general logic costs an enormous number of cells
A small truth table, typically six inputs to one output, which can implement any boolean function of those inputs
Connects the die to the outside world, with configurable voltage standards and drive strength
Stores one bit, updated on a clock edge — the thing that makes a design sequential rather than purely combinational
Drives one signal to every sequential element on the die with low and carefully balanced delay
Tens of kilobits of dedicated on-chip memory with one or two ports, far denser than the same storage built from registers
